development through operational capacity additions is highly dependent on the market environment • Entry into permitting and interconnection processes nominally requires some expenditure of capital by the project developer; these expenses alone are not sufficient to move a project from “Early Development” to “Advanced Development” status because there is still a high level of uncertainty, pending approvals, and alone result in no more than project-related paper • Projects in “Advanced Development” or “Under Construction”—progressing projects—reflect a more significant financial and human resource commitment to completion and offer a better perspective of the new capacity that may be forthcoming 4 Highlights and Takeaways • Natural gas is the largest section of the generation fleet, followed by coal and nuclear • Hydro is the oldest section of the generating fleet, followed by coal, petroleum, and nuclear • The size and age of different sections of the fleet are reflected in planned retirements of coal and nuclear plants over the next decade • The next few years of planned capacity heavily feature solar and energy storage, with natural gas at a distant third, slightly favoring non-NGCC (natural gas combined cycle), and nuclear and hydro at an even more distant fourth and fifth, respectively • Most planned additions are in early development, and renewables make up the majority of planned additions • Coal stockpiles have generally increased over the past five years, but petroleum stockpiles have remained stable after falling since 2010 5 Tracking New Power Plants and Electric Transmission Projects • This report provides a snapshot of new power plant and electric transmission activity as of December 31, 2025, based on total nameplate capacity, proposed online year (the year the project is proposed to be operational), and fuel type for power plants for the following development status categories: Status Listing Description Project has been entered in an interconnection queue, has been reported publicly, and has initiated Announced pre-permitting processes. Early Development Project has formally commenced the permitting process. Project meets two or more of the following criteria: financing has been secured; power purchase agreements have been signed; turbines have been secured; required permits have been approved; Advanced Development or an engineering, procurement, and construction contractor has signed on to the project. Site preparation may have begun. Project has commenced actual construction. Site preparation does not qualify, as a developer will Construction Begun often engage in site preparation activities to maintain project permits. Completed Project has reached commercial operation.
